claim: The ZPD is a theoretical claim: assisted performance reveals functions that are maturing. Vygotsky ran no controlled experiment for it in the cited chapter; the mental-age 12-versus-9 figures are unverified recall.
agent_test: Not testable as such; use as design rationale for sizing help.

claim: Scaffolding as a term and its six tutor functions come from Wood, Bruner and Ross 1976, not Vygotsky. The link to the ZPD was added later and critics say the two are only partly alike.
agent_test: None needed; it limits how far we may cite Vygotsky for our design.

claim: In the pyramid task (30 children, ages 3-5) unassisted success rose with age and tutors intervened more on younger children. No 3-year-old built the four-block set. Help beyond reach did not work. Numbers come via a secondary page. Gap search: 1976 PDF still not openable (403).
agent_test: Vary hint size against solver strength at equal tokens; check that help beyond reach is wasted.

claim: Contingent help (more after failure, less after success) beats fixed-level help (Wood and Middleton 1975). Only seen from memory. Gap search: page blocked (403), the DOI in b15 may be wrong (Crossref gives 10.1111/j.2044-8295.1975.tb01454.x); no LLM paper found that tests contingent escalation.
agent_test: Compare contingent hint escalation with fixed full hints at equal tokens.

claim: Computer-based scaffolding gives small-to-moderate gains in STEM: g=0.46 (144 studies, 333 outcomes) and g=0.385 (Bayesian, problem-based learning). Whether fading helps is unsettled: a 2014 preliminary version found adaptive fading better than fixed, the full 2017 paper found no effect of fading.
agent_test: Effect sizes are for human learners; do not transfer the size to the agent.

claim: Guidance beats unguided discovery, but minimal-guidance critics and expertise-reversal work say help can hurt learners who already know the material. Reversal and discovery numbers are from memory.
agent_test: Test hint level against model strength: weak help for strong models should not hurt.

claim: Human tutoring has a pooled effect of about 0.37 SD in randomised trials, stronger from trained tutors and in earlier grades. VanLehn and Ma figures are unopened.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: An LLM giving live expert-style scaffolds to human tutors raised mastery 4 points (62% to 66%, p<.01), 9 points for lower-rated tutors. Same trial in every line; versions disagree on counts (700+ vs 900 tutors; 241k, 350k or 550k messages).
agent_test: Give a weak solver expert-written lessons and measure the gain by solver strength.

claim: Unguarded GPT-4 raised practice scores (+48%) but cut later unaided exam scores (-17%, 0.054 of 1); a hint-only tutor with teacher solutions removed the harm (-0.004) but gave no gain either. GPT-4 was right only 51% of the time (42% logical, 8% arithmetic errors, 57 problems x 10 asks). About 1,000 students in about 50 classes, randomised by class. The PNAS correction (Aug 2025) only fixes an author affiliation; numbers stand. The SSRN design critique was not read.
agent_test: Measure the agent with and without access to a helper on later unaided items.

claim: A purpose-built step-by-step AI tutor beat in-class active learning in a Harvard physics crossover RCT (median post 4.5 vs 3.5; effect 0.63 by regression, 0.73 to 1.3 ceiling-corrected; enrolled N=233; median 49 min on task). One course, immediate post-test only, no retention test, no replication found.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Strong problem solvers are poor scaffolders and stock LLMs leak answers: Qwen2.5-Math-7B 0.88-0.91 on solving but 0.06 win rate on scaffolding; large general models leak 33-35% in UCO; education-tuned SocraticLM scores low on error perception.
agent_test: Count answer-leak rate when a stronger agent writes lessons for a weaker one.

claim: Simply telling a model to scaffold is unreliable: GPT-4o gained on the hard split, other models stayed flat or fell. A fuzzy-rule prompt with LLM graders gave d=0.45 on a rubric, a weak test.
agent_test: Prompt-only vs structured scaffold at equal tokens with a non-LLM scorer.

claim: Training a tutor against a simulated student with a leakage or pedagogy penalty improves tutoring: +33% predicted correctness (Scarlatos), 30.2% vs 23.5% solve without the ZPD reward (UCO), leak cuts (Dinucu-Jianu). Simulated students are imperfect.
agent_test: Use a cheap simulated solver to tune hint size before use.

claim: Stepwise hints from a helper lift small reasoning models and cost less than self-consistency (R1-Distill-Qwen-7B MATH-500 64.86% to 82.43% at 1,180 tokens vs SC 70.27% at 7,350; AIME-2024 20.69 to 68.97 while SC stayed 20.69). Figures re-opened in the full PDF. Gains are larger for weaker solvers (MATH-500: Qwen2.5-Math-7B +9.5, R1-Qwen-7B +17.6, Phi-4-mini +20.3). Untrained same-size hints hurt (Qwen2.5-Math-7B MATH-500 75.68 to 54.05). Solvers are 4B to 8B only; test sets 15 to 75 items.
agent_test: Hint scaffold vs self-consistency at equal tokens, by difficulty level.

claim: Calling the helper only at low-confidence steps keeps up to 98.9% of helper accuracy with up to 90% fewer helper tokens (SMART). This is fading in software, from one group.
agent_test: Escalation trigger on low confidence vs always-on help.

claim: In-context demonstrations act as scaffolds only for part of the queries: sorting queries into ZPD zones; selective ICL helped 6 of 8 LLaMA models; ZPD-ordered fine-tuning converged faster. One group, gains in figures. Dynamic Cheatsheet authors suggest related questions early may help but did not test order (d10).
agent_test: Route lesson retrieval to queries the agent fails alone but can solve with help.

claim: LLMs misjudge what is within a learner's reach: zero-shot level labels at or below chance for some models, fixed to 62-69% by two examples; tutors fail to redirect when learners are wrong; simulators play weak students too well.
agent_test: Check the agent's own estimate of item difficulty against measured solve rate.

claim: Stored lessons act as self-scaffolds: Reflexion HumanEval 91% vs 80%; ExpeL insights and retrieved trajectories combine; ReasoningBank +8.3 points on WebArena overall (40.5 to 48.8, Gemini-2.5-flash) and 55.1 vs about 42 for no-memory best-of-5 on Shopping; Dynamic Cheatsheet doubled Claude 3.5 Sonnet on AIME 2024 (23.3 to 50.0) but about half of that came from the empty-memory prompt (36.7); Voyager skill library. Majority vote of 3 gave no gain (23.3). Small models (Haiku, GPT-4o-mini) gain little or lose.
agent_test: Lessons memory vs none at equal tokens, across a sequence of related problems.

claim: Boundaries for stored lessons: ExpeL is below Reflexion on ALFWorld (54 vs 59) without repeats; insights vs retrieval trade places by task; the lesson writer matters (gpt-4 writer 39.0 vs gpt-3.5 writer 32.0 on HotpotQA, hand-crafted about 32.0), but writer strength is confounded with learning from experience. Induced workflows from own successes matched or beat 14 human-written ones on WebArena (35.5 vs 33.0, different harnesses). No test compares own-failure lessons with stronger-model lessons from the same writer.
agent_test: Test lesson sources: own vs stronger model vs hand-written.

claim: Self-review without an outside signal lowers accuracy; gains appear only with oracle feedback. Lessons must come from an external signal.
agent_test: Only write lessons on verified outcomes; compare with unverified lessons.

claim: A curriculum just beyond current skill drives progress: random curriculum cut Voyager discovery by 93%; STRETCH Scaffolder beat R-Zero and AZR (0.79 vs 0.72-0.73 on bargaining); ZPD-ordered fine-tuning. Domains differ.
agent_test: Order a problem set by estimated difficulty vs random at equal tokens.

claim: Teacher explanations help a weaker LLM and generalise to unexplained items (+6 points, StrategyQA); misaligned teachers hurt. Distilled chains lifted T5-XXL on GSM8K 8.11% to 21.99%.
agent_test: Check a lesson's transfer to unseen items; track harm from wrong lessons.

claim: Decomposing into ordered easier sub-questions (least-to-most) lifts compositional tasks: SCAN length 16.7% to 99.7%; GSM8K only 60.97% to 62.39% overall.
agent_test: Decompose-first vs direct at equal tokens on tasks of differing composition.

claim: Reciprocal teaching improves comprehension (median effect 0.88 on experimenter tests, 0.32 on standardised tests, 16 studies). Seen in a search snippet only.
agent_test: Weak; not used.

claim: Hints and lessons behave in opposite ways with solver strength. External hints from a stronger helper give the largest gains to the weakest solver (HintMR). Self-generated hints and stored lessons need a capable solver and give little or negative gain to small ones (Progressive-Hint, Dynamic Cheatsheet Haiku and GPT-4o-mini). Evidence covers 4B to 8B solvers for external hints, so the ladder over three or more sizes is not yet shown.
agent_test: Run hint escalation and lesson retrieval at two or more solver sizes; log gain against baseline accuracy.

claim: A bad hint-giver can lower a good solver by about 20 points. Same-size untrained hints cut Qwen2.5-Math-7B from 75.68 to 54.05 on MATH-500 (16 of 74 items) and from 46.67 to 36.00 on NuminaMath. Fine-tuned hints did not hurt. Unverified lessons carry the same risk.
agent_test: Only inject a hint or lesson from a source validated on held-out items; compare with no-hint on the same items.

claim: At equal trajectory count, stored lessons beat retries alone. ReasoningBank on WebArena Shopping (Gemini-2.5-flash, k=5): 55.1 with memory-aware scaling vs a flat 39.0 to 42.2 without memory; and 52.4 with memory but no aggregation. Dynamic Cheatsheet: majority vote of 3 gave 23.3 vs baseline 23.3 vs memory 50.0 (AIME 2024). Token-matched tests are still missing and both papers built their own method.
agent_test: Arms at equal total tokens: (a) retry only, (b) retry plus verified lessons, (c) best-of-N with verifier.

claim: The empty-memory prompt of Dynamic Cheatsheet already gave about half the gain (Sonnet AIME 2024: 23.3 to 36.7 with instructions only, 50.0 with memory; AIME 2025: 6.7 to 23.3 to 36.7). A lesson test needs an instruction-only control.
agent_test: Include a control with the same scaffold text and an empty lesson store.

claim: Evolving-playbook memory works without ground-truth labels when an execution signal exists: ACE on AppWorld 42.4 to 59.4 with labels and 57.2 without, vs ICL 46.0, GEPA 46.4, Dynamic Cheatsheet 51.9. Without any reliable feedback the authors report that ACE and Dynamic Cheatsheet can degrade.
agent_test: Gate lesson writes on a verifier or execution outcome; test with the verifier removed.

claim: Aside from Kestin, the 'does AI scaffolding persist' question has no persistence data: Bastani measured unaided performance and found harm only for the unguarded tutor; Kestin measured only an immediate post-test (N=233, one course, 0.63). No replication of Kestin or delayed retest was found.
agent_test: Background; our test is the agent run with the lesson store removed.
